reference.source: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID) / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive single-enzyme peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect caused by HSD17B4 mutations affecting the D-bifunctional protein, which carries both hydratase and dehydrogenase activities
It is the most common isolated peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect and phenotypically overlaps closely with Zellweger-spectrum disorders
Neonates typically present with profound hypotonia, neonatal-onset seizures, poor feeding, and craniofacial dysmorphism resembling Zellweger syndrome

Biochemically there is elevation of very-long-chain fatty acids together with raised pristanic acid and bile-acid intermediates (DHCA/THCA), reflecting the enzyme's role in both straight- and branched-chain oxidation
Peroxisome biogenesis is intact, so structural peroxisome assembly markers are normal and the defect is at the level of a single beta-oxidation enzyme
Diagnosis combines the biochemical profile, fibroblast enzyme/functional studies, and HSD17B4 sequencing; management is supportive
reference.pathophysiology: D-bifunctional protein deficiency arises from HSD17B4 mutations that impair the D-bifunctional protein, a peroxisomal enzyme providing the 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase and 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase steps of peroxisomal beta-oxidation for both very-long-chain and branched-chain (pristanic) fatty acids and bile-acid precursors. Loss of these activities causes accumulation of VLCFA, pristanic acid, and bile-acid intermediates. The resulting lipid toxicity and abnormal neuronal migration produce severe neonatal encephalopathy with seizures, hypotonia, and, in many cases, structural brain malformation, phenocopying the Zellweger spectrum despite normal peroxisome assembly.
additionalDifferentials: Acyl-CoA oxidase deficiency (another isolated beta-oxidation enzyme defect)
Non-ketotic hyperglycinaemia and other neonatal epileptic encephalopathies
Congenital disorders of glycosylation presenting with hypotonia and seizures
additionalInvestigations: Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids, pristanic and phytanic acids, and bile-acid intermediates (DHCA/THCA)
HSD17B4 gene sequencing to confirm the diagnosis and define the enzymatic subtype
Fibroblast studies of peroxisomal beta-oxidation and specific enzyme activities
Brain MRI to identify neuronal migration abnormalities and demyelination
EEG for characterisation of the neonatal seizure disorder
Assessment confirming intact peroxisome biogenesis (normal plasmalogens/assembly markers)
redFlags: Neonatal-onset intractable seizures with profound hypotonia
Feeding failure and failure to thrive requiring nutritional support
Structural brain malformation on imaging indicating disturbed neuronal migration
reference.prognosis: The classic presentation is severe, with most affected infants having little developmental progress, refractory seizures, and death typically within the first years of life, although milder variants with longer survival are recognised. Treatment is supportive without a disease-modifying option.
pitfalls: Diagnosing Zellweger syndrome without pursuing single-enzyme peroxisomal defects when biogenesis markers are normal
Relying on VLCFA alone and missing the branched-chain and bile-acid abnormalities that point to the bifunctional protein
Underestimating milder phenotypes that survive longer and present beyond the neonatal period
Not offering genetic counselling and carrier testing given the autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID)
management: Manage supportively through metabolic medicine and neurology, as there is no disease-modifying therapy for the underlying peroxisomal beta-oxidation defect
Treat neonatal-onset seizures with antiepileptic drugs, recognising that the epilepsy is frequently refractory
Provide feeding support, often nasogastric or gastrostomy feeding, for poor feeding and profound hypotonia
Give respiratory support and treat aspiration and recurrent chest infection as they arise
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive HSD17B4 disorder, with carrier testing and prenatal or reproductive options for the family
Involve palliative care early, given the severe prognosis with little developmental progress and death typically in the first years of life
